title: Module support, adjunctions and stalks for complementary subtopoi
statement: Let $\mathcal E$ be a Grothendieck topos [def-weil-pbc-topos], $u\hookrightarrow1_{\mathcal E}$ a subterminal object, $j:\mathcal E/u\to\mathcal E$ its open embedding, and $k:\mathcal E_c\to\mathcal E$ the complementary closed embedding of [lem-trf-topos-complement-factorization]. Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring and use modules over its constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Module inverse image along any geometric morphism between these constant-$\Lambda$ topoi is exact. Restriction $j^*$ has a module left adjoint $j_!$, and $k^*$ has module right adjoint $k_*$. The functor $k_*$ is fully faithful with essential image exactly the module sheaves $F$ satisfying $j^*F=0$. The adjunction maps identify $j^*j_!G\cong G$ and $k^*k_*H\cong H$, and $k^*j_!G=0$, $j^*k_*H=0$. For a point $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\mathcal E$ (a geometric morphism), exactly one of $p^{-1}u\cong1$ or $p^{-1}u\cong0$ holds. In the first case write $p=jp_o$, and in the second write $p=kp_c$, using the factorizations of [lem-trf-topos-complement-factorization]. For $p^{-1}u\cong1$ there are natural identifications $p^*j_!G\cong p_o^*G$ and $p^*k_*H=0$; for $p^{-1}u\cong0$ there are natural identifications $p^*j_!G=0$ and $p^*k_*H\cong p_c^*H$. Under them the counit $j_!j^*F\to F$ is the identity at an open point and the unit $F\to k_*k^*F$ is the identity at a closed point. Each point inverse image on module sheaves is exact.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero, including the module left adjoint), 0710 (lemma-stalk-j-shriek), 04EQ (lemma-stalk-exact-modules); closed support and closed-point formulas are the module consequences of sites.tex Tags 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos) and 08M1 (lemma-closed-immersion).

proof.text: For a geometric morphism between sites, inverse image on sheaves of modules over a constant commutative ring is obtained by applying the abelian inverse image and transporting the constant scalar action. The scalar comparison is canonical, and the abelian inverse image is exact; hence module inverse image is exact and is compatible with composition and localization.

Use [lem-trf-topos-localization-site-presentation] for $A=u$, so $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, $u=h_U$, and the open slice is presented by $\mathcal C/U$ with restriction as inverse image. Since $h_U$ is subterminal and the topology is subcanonical, every $V$ has at most one arrow to $U$. The coefficient identification of step 1 identifies the restricted constant ring with the constant ring on the slice. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to this ringed site. It constructs the exact module functor $j_!$ and the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$.

Compute the open adjunction unit using [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. At $V\to U$ its sole summand is $G(V\to U)$, and the unit is inclusion of that summand, hence the identity. Sheafifying and then restricting gives the same result: every covering and every refinement of an object $V\to U$ in $\mathcal C$ has its unique induced structure maps to $U$, so the matching families and their equivalence relations used in sheafification are exactly those on $\mathcal C/U$. The restricted presheaf is already $G$, a sheaf, and therefore $\eta^j_G:G\to j^*j_!G$ is an isomorphism. This also proves full faithfulness of $j_!$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), summand formula and adjunction; Tag 0F6Z (lemma-restrict-back), at-most-one-arrow case; Tag 03CY, module sheafification.

proof.text: Apply the closed-complement module statement to the complementary embedding k. Its module direct image k_* is exact and fully faithful, the counit k^*k_*H → H is an isomorphism, and its essential image is precisely the modules F whose restriction to the open subtopos is zero. Thus the unit F → k_*k^*F is an isomorphism for every module supported on the closed complement.

For a point p:Set→E, the inverse image p^{-1}u is a subterminal set, hence is either empty or singleton. These alternatives are mutually exclusive and exhaustive. The universal property of the complementary open and closed subtopoi then factors p uniquely up to the specified compatible isomorphism through j or k, respectively; write the factors as p=jp_o or p=kp_c.

The support characterization in step 3 gives $j^*k_*H=0$. For any closed module $H$, the two adjunctions give $\operatorname{Hom}(k^*j_!G,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!G,k_*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,j^*k_*H)=0$. Taking $H=k^*j_!G$ makes its identity zero, so $k^*j_!G=0$. Thus both zero restrictions hold as objects of the module categories, without any assumption that the topos has enough points.

source.place: Tags 08LY and 08M1, through the cited closed-support module theorem; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI for the open adjunction.

proof.text: For an open point use $p^*\cong p_o^*j^*$, the composition comparison of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Applying $p_o^*$ to the open unit isomorphism gives $p^*j_!G\cong p_o^*G$; applying it to $j^*k_*H=0$ gives $p^*k_*H=0$. For a closed point use $p^*\cong p_c^*k^*$ instead. The zero restriction $k^*j_!G=0$ gives $p^*j_!G=0$, and the closed counit isomorphism $k^*k_*H\to H$ gives $p^*k_*H\cong p_c^*H$. These are natural because all four identifications come from natural adjunction maps, zero objects and the natural composition comparison.

source.place: Tag 00YV, functorial inverse image; Tags 08LW and 08LY, complementary subtopoi. The resulting open point formulas agree with sites-modules.tex Tag 0710.

proof.text: Let $\epsilon^j:j_!j^*\to1$ and $\eta^k:1\to k_*k^*$ be the actual adjunction maps. The triangle identity $j^*(\epsilon^j_F)\circ\eta^j_{j^*F}=1$ shows that $j^*(\epsilon^j_F)$ is the inverse of the open unit isomorphism. Similarly $\epsilon^k_{k^*F}\circ k^*(\eta^k_F)=1$, and $\epsilon^k$ is the closed counit isomorphism, so $k^*(\eta^k_F)$ is its inverse. Apply $p_o^*$ or $p_c^*$ and the preceding composition identifications. Under exactly these identifications the counit at an open point and the unit at a closed point are identity maps, as asserted.

source.place: Tag 03DI, adjunction maps; sites.tex Tags 00YV, 08LY and 08M1. The identities are the two adjunction triangle identities.

proof.text: The point inverse image of a module sheaf is exact by the general module inverse-image result in step 1. Therefore all point inverse images on module sheaves, including p_o^* and p_c^*, are exact.

All asserted conclusions now follow from the adjunctions, support characterization, zero restrictions, point factorization and exact inverse image already established. If $u=0$, then $\mathcal E/u$ is the empty topos and $\mathcal E_c\simeq\mathcal E$, so $j_!$ is zero and $k$ is the identity. If $u=1$, then $j$ is the identity and the closed complement is the empty topos. If $\Lambda=0$, all module categories are zero. A topos with no points causes no problem: the point assertions are conditional on a given point, and the zero restrictions were proved by adjunction, not by stalk conservativity.

proof_origin.place: 03DI/03DJ for the site adjunction; 0F6Z for its subterminal unit calculation; sites.tex 03CI/04GZ for the site presentation, 00YV for inverse image, and 08LY/08M1 for the complementary closed subtopos. The point and adjunction-map formulas are the explicit categorical deductions in steps 6–8; their open part agrees with 0710.
